newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU probes Clabecq rescue plan.
newsitem.headline: EU probes Clabecq rescue plan.

text.p: The European Commission said on Wednesday it had asked Belgian authorities to provide details of the rescue plan for steelmaker Forges de Clabecq which involves a planned 1.5 billion Belgian franc capital injection and the waiving of 500 million francs in debts.
The Commission also queried a 200 million Belgian franc loan granted by Societe Wallonne de Siderurgie (SWS) to tide Clabecq over pending the result of the Commission investigation.
It was also SWS that undertook to waive a 500-million-franc loan given to the company in 1992.
The Commission said that although Belgium had taken the view that the rescue measures did not amount to state aid, it was difficult to imagine a private investor acting in the same way.
It said it stressed that the 1.5 billion capital injection, to be made by the Walloon region, had not been matched by an equivalent contributuion from the private shareholders.

"It seems very difficult to view the state assistance as equivalent to that of a private shareholder and, accordingly, to conclude that the capital increase is not state aid," the Commission said in a statement.
Belgium has one month to reply.
